fieldEvidence.excerpt: EarthDaily Analytics is a Vancouver Earth-observation company developing and commissioning an integrated satellite constellation, ground processing, analysis-ready imagery and geospatial analytics for broad-area change detection.
EarthDaily Analytics has a documented Canadian operating presence in Vancouver, British Columbia.
EarthDaily combines a multispectral satellite constellation, cloud-native processing and AI-ready imagery products to support repeatable broad-area change detection and geospatial analysis.

EarthDaily reported initial contact with EDC-08 after its July 7, 2026 launch, while EDC-02 through EDC-07 were returning initial imagery and progressing through commissioning; a separate Canadian Space Agency contribution supports an on-orbit thermal-imager demonstration through March 2027.

Daily, standardized multispectral collection and change analysis could support wide-area monitoring of northern terrain, infrastructure and maritime approaches; this is a derived fit and not a disclosed CAF deployment.

sources.summary: The federal record identifies Obruta Space Solutions Corp. in Ottawa and a 2025-2027 contribution for modular RPOD-system validation and testing.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: Obruta Space Solutions is an Ottawa space-technology company developing autonomous rendezvous, proximity-operations and docking systems for on-orbit servicing and logistics.
Obruta Space Solutions has a documented Canadian operating presence in Ottawa, Ontario.

Obruta's RPOD Kit combines spacecraft hardware and autonomous flight software for cooperative rendezvous, proximity operations and docking, including navigation-sensor fusion, safe-abort logic and mission optimization.
Autonomous rendezvous and docking software; Navigation-sensor data fusion; Built-in safe-abort logic; Compatibility with chemical and electric propulsion

NASA documentation records an autonomous docking experiment on the International Space Station in May 2025 using Obruta flight software, while Canadian Space Agency contributions support POLAR simulation work through July 2026 and modular RPOD-system validation through September 2027.

The Government of Canada records current Canadian Space Agency contributions for Obruta's RPOD simulation, validation and testing work; these awards do not establish procurement or operational adoption.
Autonomous inspection, proximity operations and sensor-driven docking are relevant to persistent robotic monitoring in orbit; this is a derived mission fit rather than a disclosed CAF deployment.
